Picking up the numbers from the worksheet I dropped in — summary of the core perf model (assumptions inline):

- Model profile: med-quant (8-bit quantized mix; KV-cache warm on 70% of requests)
- Observed single-GPU steady-state throughput: ~55 tokens/sec for an average 512-token gen at p50; p95 latency map on one GPU = ~1.8s (bad).
- Slab definition we recommend: 8 GPUs + request router + local prefix cache. With continuous batching and our optimized kernel set, effective slab throughput (user-facing) = 420 tokens/sec sustained for the med-quant profile, p95 generative latency ~180–240ms depending on concurrent KV hit rate.

Sizing math (steady & peak):
- Month 1 steady-state: 1.2M tokens/day => ~14 tokens/sec average (24h).
- Business-hours concentration (12h window, 80% traffic): avg ~56 tokens/sec in-window; 3x peak bursts observed up to 168 tokens/sec.

Therefore:
- 1 slab supports up to ~420 tps — more than enough for steady + ordinary bursts.
- For p95 <= 220ms at worst-case cache-miss bursts (3x peak + KV miss surface), we recommend 2 slabs active (840 tps aggregate) to keep per-slab scheduling latency low and batch sizes optimal.
- 3 slabs recommended if QuantumCove expects >3x month-1 growth in first 60 days or will run heavy long-context sessions (avg tokens >800).

Operational notes:
- Cold starts and cache warming: expect a 6–12 hour warmup period after deployment or after major model switch; we can pre-warm critical prefixes during rollout.
- Autoscaling time to add a slab (Dedicated burst capacity): ~6–8 hours to provision and sync KV caches across nodes; we offer burst credits for faster 2–3 hour ramps in emergency at higher cost.

I attached the SLO-fit runbook (slo-fit-runbook_v2.pdf) with the test harness we recommend to validate p95 under configurable KV-hit scenarios.

Hi Lucas — following up with commercial + next steps. Appreciate the traffic profile; based on Ben’s math here’s the suggested commercial approach so procurement can evaluate ramp risk: 

1) Pilot phase (30 days): 2 slabs reserved, monthly billing pro-rated. This provides immediate 25–30% headroom above expected Month-1 bursts and lets our engineering team run the SLO-fit validation.
2) Expansion option: add a 3rd slab with a 14-day notice for committed burst pricing (50% discounted ramp add-on vs on-demand).
3) Fallback SLA clause: If Dedicated slab capacity is constrained and we can’t provision a burst within SLAs, Redwood will: route new requests to a compatible hosted model variant (same model family, quantized) and apply a token-based rate shaping policy (we’ll provide strict error codes and retry headers for your clients).
